name: signature-hints
description: Parameter hints with theme-matched syntax highlighting, per-function exclusions, signature/doc modes and a one-key toggle.

signatureHints.enabled.description: Master switch. Toggled by the Signature Hints: Toggle command (alt+h).

signatureHints.mode.description: What the parameter hints popup shows.

enumDescriptions: Parameter names and defaults only, like JupyterLab: print(*values, sep=' ', end='\n', file=None, flush=False).
The signature exactly as the language server reports it, type annotations and return type included.
signatureHints.signatureStyle.markdownDescription: How much of the signature to show. `compact` drops type annotations and the return type, which is what keeps typed stubs (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn) from wrapping into a wall of text.

signatureHints.exclude.markdownDescription:
Calls that never show a popup. Either a flat list, or an object keyed by language id with `*` for every language:

```json
{ "python": ["print", "np.random.*"], "*": ["assert*"] }
```

Patterns are globs matched against both the bare name and the qualified name. `*` does not cross dots; use `**` for that.

signatureHints.maxDocLines.markdownDescription: Lines of documentation to keep before truncating with `…`. `0` keeps the whole docstring, which is fine because the popup scrolls: VS Code caps it at `max(editorHeight / 4, 250px)` and everything past that is reachable by scrolling.

enumDescriptions: One scrollable popup: first signature at the top, the other overloads and the documentation below it.
Show the active overload only, with the built-in 1/5 navigation buttons.
signatureHints.overloads.description: How to present multiple overloads. "all" keeps everything in one scrollable popup; "active" splits them across the widget's navigation buttons.

signatureHints.maxOverloads.description: Maximum overloads rendered when signatureHints.overloads is "all".

enumDescriptions: Leave the popup's plain header line empty.
Show the called function's name and the overload count.
signatureHints.header.description: Content of the popup's plain (non-colored) header line. The colored signature already starts with the function name, so this is off by default; VS Code always reserves the line, leaving a thin blank strip.

enumDescriptions: Color the signature using the active color theme's token colors.
Render the signature without syntax coloring.

signatureHints.monospace.markdownDescription: Render the signature in the editor's monospace font. VS Code also gives it a background pill; to remove it, set `workbench.colorCustomizations` → `textCodeBlock.background` to `#00000000`.

signatureHints.languages.description: Language ids to take over. "*" means every language.
